title: Lack of structure, mentorship and career guidance after formal education
description: People transitioning out of formal education often struggle to navigate their next career or learning stage because they lack structured guidance, accessible mentorship and clear pathways toward meaningful opportunities.
domain: Education, career development and workforce transition
environment: Transition from formal education to employment, higher education, entrepreneurship or independent skill development
additional_context: This is an exploratory problem. The affected population, root causes, severity and best intervention are not yet validated.
primary_users: People who have recently completed formal education
People who have discontinued formal education
current_process: People independently search for career options and learning resources
People may seek advice from friends, family, teachers or online communities
People attempt to identify and follow a learning or career path
where_it_occurs: During the transition from formal education into the next stage of personal and professional development
when_it_occurs: After graduation, school completion or discontinuation of formal education
workarounds: Asking friends, family or teachers for guidance
Using job portals to explore career options
pain_points: Uncertainty about what to do next
Lack of a structured learning or development roadmap
Difficulty connecting learning activities with career opportunities
root_cause_hypotheses: Formal education may not provide sufficient transition support after completion or discontinuation
Career information may be fragmented across multiple platforms
Affordable and relevant mentorship may be difficult to access
People may lack personalised guidance based on their interests, skills and circumstances
Learning resources may not clearly connect to employment or other career outcomes
constraints: Different users may have different educational backgrounds and career goals
Mentorship availability and affordability may vary
Career guidance must account for local job markets and opportunities
A proposed solution should not assume that everyone needs the same career path
assumptions: The transition out of formal education creates a meaningful guidance gap for at least some people
Some affected people would benefit from structured pathways and mentorship
The problem may affect graduates and people who discontinue education differently
unknowns: Which user segment experiences the most severe problem?
How frequently does the problem occur?
What do affected people currently do to overcome it?
Which existing solutions fail, and why?
Is the main barrier structure, mentorship, career information or access to opportunities?
Would users actually use or pay for a solution?
Which outcomes would demonstrate that the problem has been meaningfully solved?
Does the problem differ significantly across geography, education level and economic background?
